title: I built a Choose Your Own Adventure / Visual Novel generator.
author: ronin5
selftext:
You choose a genre, era, and character archetype, then the system generates a short interactive story.

  
Try it here:  
[https://www.fateweaver.net](https://www.fateweaver.net/)

Core mechanics

* One AI call generates the full graph: an 8-beat narrative with 32-page branching structure and multiple endings.
* I used gemini-2.5-flash-lite. 
* JSON validation + retry/repair loop to enforce complete structure. (Gemini seems to works better than ChatGPT in adhering to a JSON schema.) 
* Story pages are playable immediately, with choices driving path changes (good/neutral/bad arcs). 
* Additional clues and subtextual info are used for generating the images. 
* I used gpt-image-1-mini. NanoBanana was the best, but costly. 
* Local svg scene generation (procedural) as fallback if image fails. 
* Initially, I used Lyria 3 to generate the soundtrack but the 30s limit isn't enough. Ended up using Suno to generate \~60 soundtracks.

Would love feedback.  I made it for fun.

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: Do you have a lot of traffic? If so what type of demographics?

replies.author: ronin5
replies.body: No traffic.  It's the first time I'm publicly showing it.

comments.author: Fic_Machine
comments.body: It's surprisingly very polished, but the gameplay itself is not very engaging. I tried contemporary romance with hero archetype and the story went immediately to "they meet and fall in love" without much tension or build-up. I think if you narrowed down the generes to a specific kind of story, maybe detective story, maybe dungeon crawling, you could tune it to generate more interesting stories.

replies.author: ronin5
replies.body: I agree.  I was initially fascinated by unconventional mashups; but this gameplay may be limited to certain genres only.

comments.author: TiagoDev
comments.body:
Just ran through one of the stories. Pretty neat!
The music was surprisingly good!

What is your story generation structure like?

replies.author: ronin5
replies.body:
Here's a snippet:

            `REQUIRED PAGES AND EXACT NAVIGATION (you must produce ALL 32 pages with EXACTLY these nextPage values):\n` +
            `  page_1         beat 1  choices → [page_2_good, page_2_neutral, page_2_bad]\n` +
            `  page_2_good    beat 2  choices → [page_3_good, page_3_neutral]\n` +
            `  page_2_neutral beat 2  choices → [page_3_good, page_3_bad]\n` +
            `  page_2_bad     beat 2  choices → [page_3_bad, page_3_neutral]\n` +
            `  page_3_good    beat 3  choices → [page_4_good, page_4_neutral]\n` +
            `  page_3_neutral beat 3  choices → [page_4_good, page_4_bad]\n` +

replies.author: TiagoDev
replies.body: Ah! Right on. So as a player, it is about figuring out what are the good choices

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: I see. I tried doing this using prompt and letting ai drive the game.. but it felt like I lost the agency. I know ai adapt to me rather than me adapting to agent. If that is not clear that the puzzle is done upfront I would not find it true

comments.author: Savings_Count6699
comments.body:
It seems like a lot of effort has been put into this platform the User experience is smooth,  the UI and the music are nice.

I like how the prompt shows in front of you while generating the image and that report sheet at the end.

I have a question about branching the story, are all of them made momentarily as the user choose or are they predetermined when the story starts?

The closest experience to this one for me is Infinite Worlds, adding the ability to type a custom prompt for the action you are going to do. I think you can take inspiration from there.

replies.author: ronin5
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback.  It’s all predetermined when the story starts.
